name: Carbon-source minimal medium (batch, glucose) (PMC7423363)
description: Carbon-source minimal medium (batch, glucose) — medium reported in PMC7423363 (complex/undefined base — extracts not BiGG-mappable).

provenance.citation: Medium composition from PMC7423363 (see GrowthDB record).
provenance.notes: Complex medium: chemically-defined portion mapped to BiGG; biological extracts listed in `unmapped`. Added via GrowthDB curation.
provenance.verification: paper-verified (complete recipe; cited + supplementary sources chased)
provenance.base_medium: Phosphate-buffered minimal salts medium (KH2PO4/K2HPO4 + (NH4)2SO4 + 20x salt stock) supplemented with Wolfe's mineral solution and Wolfe's vitamin solution, anaerobic (100% N2, cysteine/resazurin); dextran +/- glucose carbon source.

sources_chased.what: Wolfe's mineral solution (cited as ref 52 = Wolin, Wolin & Wolfe 1963, J. Biol. Chem. 238:2882)
Wolfe's vitamin solution (cited as ref 52; standard ATCC/DSMZ composition)
sources_chased.how: WebSearch ATCC MD-VS Vitamin Supplement formulation

sources_chased.what: Main-text minimal medium recipe (Continuous culture of Kp and Bt section)

missing_before: explicit buffer identity/concentration (KH2PO4 3.85 g/L, K2HPO4 12.48 g/L)
recuration.notes: Complete minimal-medium recipe recovered from the Materials and Methods (Continuous culture section); the batch-glucose medium uses the identical minimal-medium base with 0.125-0.5% (w/v) glucose (0.5% standard). The paper's '20x methyl methanesulfonate' label is an evident naming error (MMS is an alkylating agent, not a salt stock) but the listed constituent salts (NaCl/CaCl2/MgCl2/MnCl2/CoCl2) are reported verbatim. coverage_source.definition: pct_covered_all = components / (components + unresolved ingredients) — the legacy metric, which counts pipeline-derived components as covered. pct_covered_source = source-stated components / (those + unresolved ingredients + ingredients replaced by derived components). Component classes come from tools/component_evidence_classes.tsv. A null value means the denominator was zero; it does not mean 100.
